nodes.title: MS_WORKFLOW_NOTE
widgets_values:
# Music Suite Official Workflow

ID: minimax-h3.r2v.v3-graded
Purpose: reference-to-video with joint audio.

MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo replaces MiniMaxH3ImageToVideo. There are no
keyframe inputs any more - the first/last frame loaders are gone and the
reference loaders sit in their place, outside the subgraph, promoted in
as ref_image_1..9 / ref_video_1..3 / ref_video_audio_1..3 / ref_audio_1..3.
The node additionally needs audio_vae, taken from the existing Load Audio
VAE inside the subgraph.

All reference loaders except Picture 1 ship BYPASSED. A bypassed loader
emits null and the node skips that slot, so enable only what you use
(Ctrl+B). The group is deliberately NOT brown: it must stay out of
Feature Group Toggles, or one click would enable 17 loaders that are all
still pointing at example.png.

References are addressed in the prompt as <Picture i> / <Video k> /
<Audio j>, 1-based per type, matching the loader titles. A reference you
load but never mention is still encoded and still costs tokens.

ref_image_size: 'match' scales refs to the generation's pixel area; 'max'
uses a 2048px short edge for better identity but is several times slower,
because reference tokens ride through every sampling step.

Created using Anthropic Claude - keep this line on internal
versions until a human has reviewed and verified the graph.

## Contract (titled, patchable nodes)
- MS_INPUT_TRANSFORMER_GGUF / _INT8 / _NVFP4 - the three loaders.
  MS_MODEL_SELECT picks the first one that is NOT bypassed
  (rgthree Any Switch). Same rule for MS_CLIP_SELECT.
  NOTE: there is no single MS_INPUT_TRANSFORMER node any more.
  If the Music Suite patcher resolves that exact title, point it
  at the three suffixed titles instead.
- MS_INPUT_PROMPT   - prompt text
- MS_INPUT_FIRST_FRAME / MS_INPUT_LAST_FRAME - keyframes. Each one
  passes through a Fit-To-Canvas resize driven by the SAME width /
  height as the model: an FL2VA keyframe occupies a real frame
  position and must match the target canvas.
  For first+last, un-bypass MS_INPUT_LAST_FRAME *and* its resize.
- MS_INPUT_RESOLUTION - aspect + megapixels. 0.98 MP 16:9 = 1344x768,
  which is H3's native 768 short edge. Drop to 0.4 MP for tests.
- MS_INPUT_DURATION   - seconds. MS_FRAME_COUNT snaps to 17n+5 using
  MS_INPUT_BASE_FPS (24). Do NOT feed the interpolated fps in here.
- MS_INPUT_BASE_FPS   - 24. Feeds the frame math and the muxer.
- MS_INPUT_INTERP_FPS - 60, only live when RIFE is enabled.
  MS_FPS_SELECT then hands the muxer 60 instead of 24.
- MS_INPUT_STEPS      - scheduler steps (20, simple)
- MS_INPUT_SEED       - noise seed
- MS_CACHE_1_SPECTRUM / _2_EASYCACHE / _3_H3 - chained in series.
  Bypassed nodes pass MODEL straight through, so leave exactly ONE
  un-bypassed. They sit AFTER MiniMaxH3SigmaShift.
- MS_OUTPUT_VIDEO     - h264 review copy. Master Export is the
  bypassed h265 sibling next to it.

## Model chain order
MS_MODEL_SELECT -> LoRA -> attention patch -> MiniMaxH3SigmaShift
-> cache chain -> guider / scheduler

## Required assets (ComfyUI/models/)
- diffusion_models/  MiniMax-H3-FL2VA-Q4_K_M.gguf            (active)
                     minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors
                     minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_nvfp4_convrot_int8.safetensors
- text_encoders/     qwen3vl-32B-MiniMax-H3-Q4_K_M.gguf       (active)
- vae/               minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors
                     minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors

GGUF is a community path, not the documented one. The int8_convrot
loaders are wired and ready for a same-seed A/B.

## Manual validation
1. Load in ComfyUI 0.30.0+ (native MiniMaxH3ImageToVideo required).
2. Confirm model filenames match your install.
3. Smoke test at 0.4 MP before raising resolution.
4. Queue; confirm one MP4 with video AND stereo audio under
   output/music-suite/minimax-h3/.
5. Re-export the API JSON before changing Music Suite.

nodes.title: READ ME - Attention & Cache
widgets_values:
ATTENTION - ONE MECHANISM ONLY

Currently: GGUFLoaderKJ attention = 'none',
Patch Sage Attention KJ = ON, Sol-Attn = ON.

Sage and Sol-Attn both patch attention. Pick one:
 - RTX 50-series / SM120  -> Sol-Attn, bypass the Sage patch
 - anything older         -> Sage patch, bypass Sol-Attn
   (Sol-Attn routes through flex_attention + torch.compile
    and is built for SM120)

Sol-Attn: keep exact_kv_and_rows ON. It keeps the
[text | cond | audio] prefix rows exact, and the generated
audio stream lives at the end of that prefix. Consider
dense_steps = 1 so the final denoising step runs dense -
that is where sparse approximation shows most.

CACHE CHAIN (Spectrum -> EasyCache -> H3 Cache)
Serial with bypass, so exactly ONE stays un-bypassed.
Reported on 124 frames: EasyCache ~25%, Spectrum ~15%,
and Spectrum can alter motion. Order matters - the caches
must sit AFTER MiniMaxH3SigmaShift.

subject_definitions:
<Picture 1> is the character model sheet for Hull (Drossi Trench Diver). It defines his exact appearance, proportions, suit, backpack, and anchor-hook prop.
<Picture 2> is the character model sheet for the short-haired woman. It defines her exact appearance, proportions, tactical gear, glowing orange spine, and axe.
<Picture 3> is an 8-panel cyberpunk storyboard used only as compositional and narrative reference. It defines shot order, framing, camera angles, action beats, rain atmosphere, and neon environment. Character faces, body proportions, and costume details from <Picture 3> are ignored; only the model sheets are authoritative for appearance.
<Subject 1> is Hull from <Picture 1>: lean athletic man, short dark hair, pale greenish skin, sharp features, serious expression. He wears a weathered olive-green tactical diving suit with harness straps, knee pads, utility pouches, glowing green status lights, and a large industrial backpack with coiled rope. He carries a heavy three-pronged metal anchor/hook on a rope.
<Subject 2> is the woman from <Picture 2>: athletic build, short black hair, intense dark eyes, visible neck scarring. She wears a black tactical jumpsuit with heavy harness straps, utility pouches, black combat boots, and a distinctive dark armored back plate with glowing orange-red spinal ridges. She wields a large single-bladed axe with a wrapped handle that can ignite with orange flames.

summary:
[reference generation] The target video is a high-intensity R2V cyberpunk AMV sequence set in a rainy neon-lit night city. <Picture 3> supplies only the shot structure, framing, and action progression. <Subject 1> and <Subject 2> are realized strictly from <Picture 1> and <Picture 2>; any facial or costume differences present in the storyboard panels are discarded.

retention_analysis:
<Picture 1> (character design for <Subject 1>): fully_preserved - face, suit, green lights, backpack, and anchor-hook match the model sheet exactly.
<Picture 2> (character design for <Subject 2>): fully_preserved - face, short hair, neck scarring, black tactical gear, glowing orange spine, and axe match the model sheet exactly.
<Picture 3> (storyboard structure for all shots): weak_reference - only panel order, camera angles, subject placement, rain, and neon environment are followed. Facial likeness, exact body proportions, and costume details from the storyboard are ignored.
<Subject 1> (appears throughout): fully_preserved - appearance taken exclusively from <Picture 1>.
<Subject 2> (appears throughout): fully_preserved - appearance taken exclusively from <Picture 2>. The axe gains temporary flame effects during combat.

detailed_description:
The target video is a cinematic cyberpunk AMV rendered in the gritty anime style of Chainsaw Man: rough expressive linework, high-contrast lighting, heavy use of solid blacks, stark shadows, and a slightly dirty, high-impact aesthetic with dynamic motion and weighty action.
[Shot 1] Wide high-angle shot of a rainy neon city rooftop at night. <Subject 1> kneels at the edge of a concrete ledge, back partially to camera, looking out over a glowing canal and distant skyscrapers. Heavy rain falls; cyan and magenta neon signs pulse on the buildings below. Camera slowly pushes in.
[Shot 2] At 00:01.800, hard cut to extreme close-up of <Subject 2>’s face (model-sheet likeness from <Picture 2>). Rain streaks down her short black hair and across the visible scarring on her neck. Her intense dark eyes stare directly toward camera under harsh neon pink and cyan light. Expression is hard and focused.
[Shot 3] At 00:03.200, cut to medium shot of <Subject 1> standing in a narrow rainy alley, full body visible in the olive-green diving suit with glowing green lights. He holds the rope of his metal anchor-hook loosely in one hand, posture ready. Neon signs in Japanese and Chinese characters glow on the walls behind him. Rain pours.
[Shot 4] At 00:04.600, dynamic three-quarter shot of <Subject 2> in a low combat crouch. Her black tactical gear and glowing orange spine are clearly visible. She has just landed or slid through a large splash of water on the wet street, water erupting around her boots and axe. Orange-red light from the splash and her spine illuminate the rain.
[Shot 5] At 00:06.000, close-up of <Subject 1>’s face (model-sheet likeness from <Picture 1>), slight smirk, hand raised to his chin in a thoughtful gesture. Green suit collar and glowing lights frame his face. Heavy rain and neon bokeh behind him.
[Shot 6] At 00:07.200, medium shot focused on <Subject 2>’s torso and arms as she grips the flaming orange axe with both hands. The blade burns brightly, steam and sparks rising where the fire meets the rain. Her glowing orange spine ridges pulse. Camera is slightly low and angled upward.
[Shot 7] At 00:08.600, fast tracking shot following <Subject 2> as she charges forward through the rain, swinging the flaming axe in a wide arc. Sparks and orange trails streak behind the blade. <Subject 1> is visible further down the wet street, bracing with the anchor-hook raised, ready to intercept. Neon reflections streak across the pavement.
[Shot 8] At 00:10.400, low-angle shot of <Subject 2> bringing the flaming axe down hard onto the wet street. A massive explosion of orange sparks, steam, and water erupts upward around the impact point. <Subject 2>’s silhouette is framed against the rising fire and neon city lights. In the same frame, <Subject 1> is seen from the back on the right side of the shot, taking a sharp step backward to dodge the descending axe as it hits the ground.

overall_soundscape:
Constant heavy rain and distant city traffic. Wet footsteps and fabric movement. Sharp metallic clink of the anchor-hook. Whoosh and crackle of the flaming axe. Deep impact boom and sizzling steam on the final strike. Occasional distant neon sign buzz and wet tire hiss.

non_diegetic_music:
Dark electronic AMV track with pulsing low-end synth bass, sparse industrial percussion that hits on the action cuts, rising tension pads during the chase, and a sharp distorted impact hit synced to the final axe strike. No vocals.

nodes.title: READ ME - Post Grade
widgets_values:
POST GRADE + PIPELINE FIXES (v3)
Created using Anthropic Claude - keep this note on internal versions
until the settings have been reviewed/verified.

PATH:
  VAEDecode -> RIFE -> FILM Net -> HDR -> LUT -> Trim -> Bloom
    -> Upscaler -> Sharpen -> VideoCombine

EVERYTHING IS GROUP-TOGGLEABLE. Bypass = passthrough, so any stage
you switch off in Feature Group Toggles simply hands its input on.
That is why the Any Switch was removed: a BYPASSED node still emits
an image, so 'Any Switch' always picked branch 1 and the FILM Net
result was computed and thrown away. Chaining in series is the
pattern that actually matches how the group bypasser works.
  - Do NOT enable RIFE and FILM Net at the same time. They stack
    (24 -> 60 -> 120) and the fps below will not match.

ATTENTION - both can and should be on, in this order:
  LoRA -> Sage-Attn -> Sol-Attn -> SigmaShift
Sol-Attn reads any existing optimized_attention_override and chains
onto it: it takes eligible sparse self-attention and delegates the
rest (cross-attn, short seqs, steps outside its sigma window) to
Sage. The old order had Sage last, which overwrote Sol-Attn
entirely. Verify in the console - you should now see:
  [sol_attn] chaining onto an existing attention override
If that line is missing, the order is wrong again.

FPS (MS_FPS_SELECT priority: first non-null wins):
  any_01 RIFE      60   (lives in the RIFE group)
  any_02 FILM Net  48   (lives in the FILM group, = 24 x2)
  any_03 base      24
Disabled groups emit null, so the right fps follows the toggle.
If you change FILM's multiplier, change 48 to match.

ADDING NEW TOGGLEABLE GROUPS:
The 'Feature Group Toggles' node has matchColors = brown. rgthree
resolves that to #b06634 and SKIPS every group with any other
colour. A new group must be brown or it will not appear in the
toggler (this is also why 'Video Options', which is green, has
never shown up there).

GRADE TUNING (change one at a time):
 1 Pseudo-HDR  hdr_intensity 0.45. Above ~0.8 goes haloed.
 2 LUT         strength 0.7. 0.4-0.5 if skin goes too gold.
 3 Trim        saturation/contrast +10-15 finishing pass.
 4 Bloom       bypassed; most memory-hungry node here.
 5 Sharpen     alpha 0.35 subtle, 0.6+ crunchy. Stays after the
               upscaler so it works at final resolution.

The grade runs BEFORE the upscaler: same look, ~1/4 the CPU cost
(~2.0 s/frame -> ~0.5 s/frame at 124 frames).

Requires Worlds_AMV_Style.cube in ComfyUI/models/luts/ and
colour-science in python_embeded. The LUT is an algorithmic
approximation of the Riot Worlds look, not an official Riot asset.
